title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Cases of Compensation for Personal Injury Caused by Electric Shock

articles.content_en: Article 1 The "high voltage" as stipulated in Article 123 of the General Principles of the Civil Law includes high voltage electricity of 1 kilovolt (KV) and above; voltage levels below 1 kilovolt (KV) are non-high voltage.

Article 2 For cases where personal injury is caused by high voltage electricity, the owner of the electric power facility shall bear civil liability in accordance with Article 123 of the General Principles of the Civil Law.
However, where personal injury caused by high voltage electricity results from multiple causes, the respective liabilities shall be determined according to the causal force between the tortfeasor's act and the damage result. Where the tortfeasor's act is the main cause of the damage consequences, [the tortfeasor] shall bear primary liability; where the tortfeasor's act is not the main cause of the damage consequences, [the tortfeasor] shall bear corresponding liability.

Article 4 The scope of compensation for personal injury caused by electric shock includes:
(1) Medical expenses: refers to the fees charged by the hospital for treating the party injured by electric shock. Medical expenses shall be determined on the basis of the diagnosis certificate, prescriptions, and bills for medical fees and hospitalization expenses issued by the treating hospital.
Medical expenses shall also include expenses for continued treatment, functional training of other organs, and appropriate plastic surgery expenses. Expenses for continued treatment may be determined either by a lump-sum judgment based on the case circumstances, or by setting the standard for compensation according to treatment needs.
The calculation of expenses shall refer to the standards for publicly-funded medical care.
The hospital chosen by the party shall be a medical institution established according to law and having the corresponding treatment capacity, such as hospitals, health centers, and first-aid stations. The party shall choose a nearby treatment hospital based on the extent of injury and treatment needs.
(2) Lost working time compensation: For those with fixed income, it shall be calculated based on the actual reduction in income. For those without fixed income or with no income, it shall be calculated based on the average annual wage of employees in the location of the accident in the preceding year. The period of lost working time may be determined based on the certificate from the medical institution or forensic identification; if it cannot be determined thereby, it may be determined based on the actual extent of injury and recovery status of the victim.
(3) Hospitalization food subsidy and nutrition expenses: Hospitalization food subsidy shall be calculated based on the time the victim is hospitalized or receiving treatment away from home, with reference to the standard for food subsidy for ordinary staff of state organs on business trips in the location of the accident. The People's Court shall decide whether to compensate for nutrition expenses and the amount based on the victim's disability condition and the opinion of the treating hospital.
(4) Nursing expenses: During the victim's hospitalization, if the nursing personnel have income, the expenses shall be calculated in accordance with the provisions on lost working time compensation; if they have no income, the expenses shall be calculated based on the average cost of living in the location of the accident. They may also be calculated with reference to the market price of nursing workers. After the victim is discharged from the hospital, if nursing is still needed, the expenses shall be determined based on the certificate of the treating hospital and the disability grade. Expenses for disability equipment shall be considered together.
(5) Living subsidy for disabled persons: It shall be calculated based on the extent of loss of working capacity or the disability grade, according to the average cost of living in the location of the accident. From the month when the disability is determined, compensation shall be paid for twenty years. However, for persons aged fifty or above, the period shall be reduced by one year for each additional year of age, but shall not be less than ten years; for persons aged seventy or above, the period shall be calculated as five years.
(6) Expenses for disability equipment: If a disabled victim needs to be fitted with prosthetics, mobility aids, or other assistive devices out of necessity for daily life or to assist in production and labor, the expenses shall be calculated based on the cost of ordinary domestic equipment with a hospital certificate.
(7) Funeral expenses: If there are provisions by the relevant state or local authorities, they shall be followed; if there are no such provisions, the expenses shall be calculated based on the reasonable expenses actually incurred for holding the funeral.
(8) Death compensation: It shall be calculated based on the local average cost of living, with compensation for twenty years. For persons aged seventy or above, the period shall be reduced by one year for each additional year of age, but the compensation period shall not be less than ten years.
(9) Living expenses for dependents: It shall be limited to persons who were actually supported by the deceased before their death or by the disabled person before losing working capacity and who have no other source of income, and shall be calculated based on the basic living expenses standard for local residents. If the dependent is under eighteen years of age, living expenses shall be calculated up to the age of eighteen. If the dependent has no working capacity, living expenses shall be calculated for twenty years, but for persons aged fifty or above, the period shall be reduced by one year for each additional year of age, but the period for calculating living expenses shall not be less than ten years; if the dependent is aged seventy or above, the support expenses shall be calculated for only five years.
(10) Transportation expenses: refers to the reasonable transportation expenses actually necessary for rescuing the victim of electric shock, including the necessary transportation expenses for mandatory transfer to another hospital for treatment.
(11) Accommodation expenses: refers to the expenses for local accommodation when the victim cannot be hospitalized or stay at home due to objective reasons and must find accommodation on site. The amount shall be determined with reference to the standard for accommodation expenses for ordinary staff of state organs on business trips in the location of the accident. For the transportation expenses, lost working time compensation, accommodation expenses, and food subsidy incurred by the party's relatives and friends in participating in the handling of the electric shock accident, they shall be calculated with reference to the relevant provisions of the preceding paragraph, but the number of persons for which expenses are calculated shall not exceed three.

Article 5 For the various expenses calculated in accordance with the preceding article, those that have actually been incurred and are urgently needed by the victim shall be paid in a lump sum; for other expenses, the time and method of payment may be determined based on factors such as the amount, the degree of need of the victim, and the performance capacity of the party. If the method of periodic payment compensation is adopted, the amount of each installment shall be determined and the person liable shall be required to provide appropriate security.
Article 6 Compensation for personal injury caused by non-high voltage electricity may be handled by reference to the provisions of Articles 4 and 5.
